note: The highest prompt–description similarity in the set. Most English listeners mention country (5 of 7) and a female singer (6 of 7).
ko_tr: Pop music with a female vocalist. The band instruments and the vocal blend well, and the standout is a singer who sings really well.
It has an American country feel. Like a performance staged in a wide cornfield, filmed by a drone from far away.
An English-language song with a sweet, lilting female vocal over band music; 1990s-style music that comes across as yearning.
Typical 80s female-vocal pop; the open, soaring sound feels good.
An exciting pop song by a woman; a strong guitar beat and a female vocal, with an upbeat, cheerful mood.
A strong, bright female vocal over a rock sound; music that brings a moving finale to mind.
A song at a moderate tempo that anyone could enjoy; an emotional female vocalist who sings well; hopeful and comfortable.

note: The prompt is a short story with no musical terms. No listener mentions being sick; three of eight English listeners pick up on video games.
ko_tr: A slight cyberpunk atmosphere, but the setting isn't the future. A song that would play in the background at a huge futuristic corporation's conference, in a city or building with a futuristic concept, as a wealthy host appears.
Sounds like a small local band that British boys formed before they grew up. Upbeat yet dreamy, with a striking synthesizer.
A bubbly song with a high male vocal. The beat is regular and easy to move to; music you might listen to when making a fresh start.
The main character persuades colleagues one by one and builds a team. The band sound adding one part at a time is like team building.
A song that suits driving: an intense drum beat and a man's low, attractive, calm voice.
A male vocal that feels low and subdued. The melody and rhythm are bright and fast, but the repeating rhythm makes it feel calm.
Band music that uses synthesizer to bring out the melody, fitting for when a film's end credits roll.

note: Listeners hear the groove and the saxophone, but their genre labels range from swing jazz to rock to tropical house. Nobody mentions four men or New York.
ko_tr: Drums, bass, electric guitar and electric piano work together, with a groovy male vocal standing out.
A groove-filled band number where percussion, electric guitar and male vocal combine perfectly.
Feels like light rock merged with a funky style. A song with a rebellious-sounding male vocal. An electric guitar melody that gives a funky, country-ish feel.
It's soul-funk: the vocal lays down a groovy line while a guitar solo carries the song along behind it. The vocal hits hard, and the bassline sits heavy underneath.

note: Both groups hear a slow guitar piece with no vocals. English listeners keep returning to “melancholic” (5 of 7); Korean listeners more often write about calm (차분, 잔잔) and about where they would listen: a rainy autumn day with coffee, a summer evening, a campfire.
ko_tr: The guitar flows loosely, as if the melody runs on without clear beat divisions. No vocals; it feels led by a classical guitar melody. Seems to be a duo or more.
Music combining an acoustic guitar melody with strumming; soft and lyrical.
Gentle guitar music that would be nice to listen to over a cup of coffee on a rainy autumn day.
Music built on an acoustic guitar melody, with a calm yet emotional atmosphere. No vocals; a melody that seems sad and is beautiful.
A gentle instrumental in which traditional classical guitars stack up harmonies as they play.
The quiet and calm of a soft guitar melody. With only guitar and no vocals, it evokes the idle ease of resting on a summer evening.
Sweet guitar sound that suggests a song for a trip or camping; a lonely, calm mood, like someone playing alone to ease their loneliness, or playing for people around a campfire.

note: The prompt says heavy metal and never says rock. Five of six English listeners and four of seven Korean listeners call it rock. Across the full set, metal → rock is one of the strongest prompt–description word associations (χ² = 134.59).
ko_tr: Intense rock music in which drums and guitar blend with the vocal, giving a mournful feeling.
Classic rock that is all 90s, but now with a side of a tasty German vocal line.
A song sung by a male vocalist over guitar and drums. A minor-sounding melody that isn't bright.
An old-pop feel like Hotel California, with intense rock vocals and electric guitar. Feels like a rock ballad at an unhurried tempo.
A rough vocal with acoustic instruments creating a grand, dramatic atmosphere; an epic-feeling song.

A typical chanson feel, sung by a male vocalist with a somewhat rough, hoarse voice. A medium tempo that doesn't drag. It feels like the climax of the whole song; you can feel the expressiveness of a male vocal that seems to cry out its emotions.
Rock music with a husky vocal, good for moving along to at a rock festival.

note: Listeners name the rap they hear (6 of 7 English, 5 of 6 Korean) rather than the hip-hop label in the prompt; two English listeners also catch the UK drill. Across the full set, hip-hop → rap is the second-strongest association (χ² = 184.04).
ko_tr: A hip-hop/rap song. The man raps fast, then slow. It goes slow rap, then fast rap, and the lyrics in each part are the same.
A song you might hear in a UK dubstep or bass club; the a cappella would very likely get layered onto other tracks too.
Tension-building sounds and rap. Good for when conflict escalates in a film or game.
Music where the rap part stands out and a simple melody keeps repeating; the ringing, bell-like instrument is striking.
Fast, underground-feeling English hip-hop in which a low male vocal raps quickly and, in between, gets the crowd to call back with lines like “I say, you say.”
A robotic-sounding, effected vocal starts the song rapping, then another vocal comes in and lays down a melody. A hard-hitting song where the two vocals trade raps back and forth.
